message.content: {"thought": "Now I have a clear picture. The hardware has 16 homogeneous WS chiplets in a 4x4 grid, each with 4096 compute units and 8192 buffer size. Total compute = 65536 units. The FFN1 tilings are ~99.99% compute-bound with ~14.5B latency each, and there are 16 FFN1 tilings. The tensor parallelism is 16 (matching chiplet count), so each chiplet handles one tiling. The compute units per chiplet (4096) may be insufficient for the FFN1 GEMM, causing the high compute latency. The 68.5% average utilization suggests scheduling imbalance across chiplets. I have enough evidence to diagnose the bottleneck state. Let me finish with a structured diagnosis.", "action": "finish", "finish_reason": "Sufficient evidence gathered. FFN1 tilings are purely compute-bound (99.99% compute time, 98.4% compute energy) with ~14.5B latency each, driven by 4096 compute units per WS chiplet being insufficient for the FFN1 GEMM workload. FFN2 tilings are compute-bound in time but memory/communication-dominated in energy, appearing at critical-path end. Critical-path-end layers (norm2, res2) are memory/communication-bound. Average core utilization of 68.5% indicates scheduling imbalance across the 16 homogeneous WS chiplets (4x4 grid, tensor_parall=16). The primary bottleneck is compute resource starvation for FFN1 tilings, with secondary memory/communication pressure on FFN2 and norm/residual layers, plus load imbalance."}
